function: Joint learned pilot design, downlink channel estimation and CSI feedback with a Swin Transformer (SWTCAN); VAE-generated pretraining and AirComp federated fine-tuning (p. 1, p. 2).
system: FDD massive MIMO, 256-antenna UPA (16x16) base station, single-antenna UEs, OFDM with 256 subcarriers, 28 GHz; no RIS (p. 2, p. 4).
method: Swin Transformer autoencoder (SWTCAN) trained end-to-end on NMSE; VAE sample generator for pretraining; federated fine-tuning (FedAMS) of 11% of parameters via AirComp (p. 3, p. 4).
data_channel: Sionna CDL-A, CDL-B, CDL-C from 3GPP [20], 28 GHz; 6000 training, 2000 validation, 2000 test samples; 120 high-quality CDL-B samples for adaptation (p. 4, p. 5).
test_conditions: Fig. 2: train and test on CDL-B. Pretrain on 6000 CDL-A, adapt with 120 CDL-B samples, test on 2000 CDL-B; federated-tuning with 600 UEs (p. 4, p. 5).
baselines: Learned: Transformer CE+feedback [18], MMV-LAMP CE [32], CsiNet feedback [33]; oracles with perfect CE or feedback; centralized learning versus federated-tuning (p. 4, p. 5).
metrics: NMSE (dB) versus feedback bits B and uplink communication overhead; FLOPs and computation time of federated-tuning versus centralized learning (p. 4, p. 5).
complexity: Order O(LPN_BS C^2+LW^2PN_BS C) ~1.4e7 versus Transformer 1.5e8, MMV-LAMP 1.1e10, CsiNet 2.4e6; 2.6e9 FLOPs per global epoch; 3.6e6 tuned parameters (p. 4, p. 5).
openness: Code stated as publicly available at https://gaozhen16.github.io/ (author homepage); no separate dataset link (p. 1).
q1_support: p. 4: "the CDL channel models are adopted from 3GPP standards [20]"; [20] is 3GPP TR 38.901 (p. 6), and the same CDL channels are used for training and testing.
q2_support: p. 5: "Scheme C: We pre-train SWTCAN with 6000 CDL-A samples, fine-tune it with 120 CDL-B samples."; the schemes are tested on 2000 CDL-B samples, the cell distribution.
q3_support: p. 4: "Baseline 1: The Transformer-based network for CE and CSI feedback [18]"; baselines are learned ([18], [32], [33]) or oracles with perfect CE or feedback, and no classical non-learned estimator or feedback scheme is compared.
q4_support: p. 4: "The complexity of the proposed SWTCAN mainly comes from W-MSA or SW-MSA layers", given as an order of about 1.4e7; Table II (p. 5) gives FLOPs.
q5_support: p. 1: "Our code is publicly available at https://gaozhen16.github.io/"
notes: Area 2: SWTCAN does pilot design, channel estimation and CSI feedback (p. 2); AirComp only fine-tunes this model (p. 3-4), so area 7 does not apply. q3 is borderline: the perfect-CE and perfect-feedback baselines (p. 4) are oracles, not classical methods, so the reviewer should confirm. The q5 link is an author homepage rather than a repository, so the reviewer should confirm the code is there.
